value: It lies on a main sea route where ships stop to refuel, take water and provisions

value: The claim that leave of the House is required to move a censure motion is the incorrect statement
reasoning: A censure motion is a substantive motion: the Speaker decides whether it is in order, it must state its grounds, and it can be moved against one minister, a group of ministers or the whole Council of Ministers, so C and D are correct. Unlike a no-confidence motion, it does not need the leave of the House (the backing of 50 members), so A is the incorrect statement. Runner-up: B, if the setter holds that the Speaker, not the Government, fixes the time for its discussion.

value: A Money Bill can be referred to a joint committee of the two Houses (incorrect)
reasoning: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and the Speaker's certificate on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final (Article 110). When the Speaker's office is vacant, the Deputy Speaker performs the Speaker's duties, including certification. A Money Bill is never sent to a joint committee of both Houses, because the Rajya Sabha has only a recommendatory role on it, so D is the incorrect feature.

value: All three: equal treatment balanced with proportionality, due and equal consideration for all, and recognition of special needs
reasoning: The standard account of social justice (as in the NCERT Political Theory text) rests on equal consideration for every individual, equal treatment of equals balanced against the principle of proportionality, and going beyond equal treatment to recognise special needs. All three statements match this. Runner-up: B (1 and 3), if statement 2 is read as the older idea of 'giving each his due' rather than a requirement of social justice.

value: The Attorney-General has right of audience in all courts in India, not only the Supreme Court and High Courts
reasoning: Under Article 76 the Attorney-General must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge, holds office during the pleasure of the President and receives remuneration the President decides. Article 76(3) gives the Attorney-General right of audience in all courts in the territory of India, so limiting it to the Supreme Court and High Courts is wrong.

value: Both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate on Concurrent List subjects

value: 1 and 3: Parliament can legislate on State List subjects in some circumstances, e.g. after a Rajya Sabha resolution backed by two-thirds present and voting

value: Both: ordinances are temporary, and lapse unless Parliament approves them within six weeks of reassembly
reasoning: Under Article 123 the President can promulgate ordinances only when Parliament is not in session, and they are temporary laws. value: Milpa-Mexico, Ladang-Malaysia, Roca-Brazil, Masole-Zaire

value: Biosafety, under the Convention on Biological Diversity

value: Ecotone

value: All three statements about sulh-i kul are correct
reasoning: Sulh-i kul, Akbar's ideal, means 'absolute peace'. Under it all religions and schools of thought had freedom of expression, provided they did not undermine the state's authority or fight among themselves. Abul Fazl describes it being implemented through state policies such as granting titles to nobles of all backgrounds and abolishing the pilgrimage tax and jizya.

value: The claim that not all Mughal emperors gave grants for places of worship is incorrect

The pilgrimage tax was abolished in 1563 and the jizya in 1564, Akbar instructed officers to follow religious toleration, and Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb issued grants to repair temples damaged in war.

Meluhha is the name Mesopotamian texts probably used for the Harappan region, and since the script cannot be read, nothing in it is known to refer to Meluhha.
